For any rational R on P^1 with residue-carrying set N, all 2^|N|-2 groupings of N into two blocks are EQUIVALENT to the single relation sum_{p in N} Res_p R = 0: adding the complement sum to one side returns it, subtracting returns the grouping. So the groupings span a rank-1 space of relations and carry ONE identity between them. Hence the u->infinity tie family (cardinality > 1) CANNOT be indexed by the groupings of a single R; the brief's 'enumerate the 2^3-2 = 6 identities at |S|=2' was counting bracketings of one relation. Sum-of-all-residues = 0 checked 18/18 exact as a sanity control.

The index set of the residue theorem for R_{s,t} = z^{t-s} prod_{k<s}(z-w_k) P/D is NOT the pole set, and this is an independent error in Q553's premise. PROVED: N(S,s,t) is contained in {w_m : m in S, m >= s} u {0 if t<s} u {inf if t>=0}. Three unconditional memberships: every w_m with m >= s (D's zero is simple and Q_s(w_m) != 0); 0 at t = s-1 (residue = (Q_s P/D)(0) != 0); inf at t = 0 (R ~ e_S/z so Res_inf = -e_S != 0 -- note inf is then a ZERO of R, not a pole, yet carries a residue: that is the off-by-one). Poles w_m with m < s are CANCELLED by Q_s, matching the vanishing of rho(s,w_m,w) in Psi's own head factor.

The reverse inclusion (0 carries a residue for all t<s, inf for all t>=0) is a coefficient-non-vanishing statement, true off a proper subvariety, not universal. Measured: predicted set == measured set as SETS, BOTH DIRECTIONS, 60/60 at random rational points (|S|=3,4; s<=3; t in -2..2). Recorded as computed, not proved; the unconditional cases live in clio-Q553-residue-carrier-inclusion.

What replaces the grouping family. Phi[g] = -Res_0[g/D] - Res_inf[g/D] for every Laurent g (simple zeros of D at w_m != 0, then the residue theorem), so the family is indexed by the TEST FUNCTION f, one relation per f, and {z^a} is a basis. I_a := Phi[z^a P] = e_S Psi_{(1),a+1}(S); R_{s,t} has f = z^{t-s}Q_s, in the span of {z^a : t-s <= a <= t-1}, triangular with UNIT diagonal, so the (s,t)-family is a re-basing, not a new family. sigma_{1/w} = 1/sigma_w and sigma_w(1/z) = 1/(e_S^2 sigma_w(z)) (both by direct product manipulation; the second is D/(e_S P)). Hence I_a(1/w) = -I_{-2-a}(w) for all a: substitute, use 1/sigma_w(z) = e_S^2 sigma_w(1/z), and pair G(z) = z^a sigma_w(1/z) with F(z) = z^{-a-2} sigma_w(z) via G(1/u)/u^2 = F(u) and F(1/u)/u^2 = G(u), which swaps Res_0 and Res_inf with a sign. THE HEADLINE, and it needs no residues at all. rho(k,X,w) = prod_{l<k}(1 - w_l/X) = X^{1-k} Q_k(X), so rho(k_j,X_j,w) X_j^{th_j} = X_j^{th_j-k_j+1} Q_{k_j}(X_j); expanding each Q_k(X) = sum_i (-1)^{k-1-i} e_{k-1-i}(w_1..w_{k-1}) X^i and exchanging the finite sums with the head sum (every other factor of Psi is independent of kappa,theta) gives Psi_{kap,th}(M) = sum_{i_1..i_r} prod_j [(-1)^{k_j-1-i_j} e_{k_j-1-i_j}(w_1..w_{k_j-1})] Psi_{(1^r),th'}(M), th'_j = th_j - k_j + 1 + i_j. EVERY head length collapses to length 1, for every r -- so this component of Q551 (does the one-head form lift to multi-head) is answered YES, elementarily. Verified r=1 400/400 in pure Fractions (an independent mechanism from the sympy residue route), r=2 175/175, r=3 36/36. Two live negative controls: drop the per-head sign -> 0/20 on live samples; shift the head window to w_2..w_s -> 0/18. Combined with the closed-form table this is a closed form for Psi_{(s),t} at EVERY (s,t) (160/160), strictly stronger than the residue form, and it decouples the head data (w_1..w_{s-1}) from S entirely.

Grouping the head-injection sum by its underlying r-subset T turns the only order-dependent factor into a Vandermonde: prod_{j<k}(1 - x_{pi(j)}/x_{pi(k)}) = sgn(pi) prod_{i<k}(x_k-x_i) / prod_k x_{pi(k)}^{k-1}, so the ordered contribution of T is det(x_i^{m_j}) / prod_{i<k}(x_k - x_i) with m_j = theta_j + j - 1. Hence Psi_{(1^r),th}(M) = sum_{|T|=r} B(T) det(x_i^{m_j})/Vandermonde(T), B(T) = prod_{x in T}(1-x^-2) prod_{{x,y} in T}(1-1/xy) prod_{t in M-T} prod_{x in T}(1-1/(w_t x))/(1-w_t/x). When the m_j are distinct the alternant is +-s_mu(T), so Psi is a B-weighted sum of SCHUR polynomials over r-subsets -- and with head collapse, so is every Psi_{kap,th}.
